deviations.what: t15 writes a route name (e.g. 'lobes gateway') into provenance.endpoint instead of copying the Atlas's endpoint URL; the data contract refuses any endpoint that looks like a network address (endpoint-is-address)
deviations.reason: An Atlas records its endpoint as a URL, and the spec rule is that the embedding gateway address never reaches a page; copying it as t15's criterion words it would break that rule. User chose 'Name only' on 2026-11-13.

deviations.what: t15 adds two registration lines (the import and _export_cmd.register(sub)) to embeddings/cli/__init__.py in embeddings-cli, a stable-contract module; no parser behaviour, dispatch, _errors.py or _output.py changes
deviations.reason: A new verb can only be registered in _build_parser() in that module, at the spot embeddings-cli's CLAUDE.md marks for it; criterion 5's 'no stable-contract module changes' cannot be met literally without hiding the registration inside another verb. User chose 'Accept the 2 lines' on 2026-11-13.

deviations.what: An extra performance pass, not a task in the plan, reworks three merged modules: the principal-direction fit becomes a sliced stepper (t4), the modes prepare in units under about 4 ms (t7), and an append no longer copies all base vectors (t5). Results must stay bit-identical and the frozen data contract is unchanged.
deviations.reason: The user's live test showed a visible jump after appending points (measured: one frame of about 200 ms at 384-d when Tumble refits, 888 ms at 10,500 x 1024) and a heavier initial load on phone Safari; t8's criterion says an append must not reset the camera, and the spec says no visible jump where avoidable. The plan's tasks t4, t5 and t7 did not bound these costs.

deviations.what: embeddings export gains --group-by <key> (writes each point's group from a metadata key) and writes only the corpus file's name in provenance.params
deviations.reason: t16 found a real export is one colour with no group names, and carried a local absolute path; user approved the group option on 2026-11-14

deviations.what: Lattice draws hidden directions from the data's 8 strongest principal directions instead of the full space (mode option hidden: 'full' keeps the reference's rule); the light-background default becomes 'soft'
deviations.reason: t16 measured Lattice at 1.126 group separation on real vectors, equal to a random frame; user said 'build' on 2026-11-14, and at sign-off accepted only the soft light style

evidence.test_ref: js/test/viewer.test.js::mount appends exactly one child to the element and touches nothing else
evidence.behavior_text: One child is added; body, head, classes, styles and window keys are unchanged. Sibling tests assert replace, append keeping the camera, and a plain message on invalid data; tests/browser/test_viewer_render.py asserts the same in Chromium.
evidence.contract_text: mount attaches a viewer to exactly the element given and touches nothing outside it; update with a full set replaces the view, update with an append adds points and keeps the camera and existing points; neither call throws on valid data, and invalid data yields a plain message in the element, not an exception in the host.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: 'neither call throws on valid data' is implicit only (no test states it); no negative control for 'camera kept'.

evidence.behavior_text: Across three delivery forms every logged request is on the test server's origin; test_c2_no_csp_violation asserts zero violations under script-src 'self'; tests/test_standalone_page.py asserts every asset is a shipped same-folder name.
evidence.contract_text: The file makes no request to any origin, contains no inline script requirement, and works under script-src 'self'; fonts and every other asset come from the host or from the file itself.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green, and negative controls show each check fails when broken (test_harness_negative_controls.py, test_check_no_external_origin.py::test_negative_control_bites). The tests assert 'no other origin'; the shells do read the data file from their own origin.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/web-component-static.test.js::the web component calls only mount, update and destroy on the core
evidence.behavior_text: Only T.mount, T.update and T.destroy are used on the core object, and the web component holds no graphics or projection code (16 mutations are caught).
evidence.contract_text: Both shells call only the public mount/update/destroy API of the same unmodified core file; neither carries its own copy of rendering or projection logic.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green with a negative control, for the web component only. Partly covered: the standalone page script also uses api.sample and handle methods (its test allows that), and no test scans page.js for rendering or projection code.

evidence.behavior_text: After 20 mount/destroy cycles in Chromium, canvases, live contexts, pending frames, timers, observers and listeners equal the baseline; unit tests assert no frame work while hidden or off screen and a message on context loss.
evidence.contract_text: destroy(el) releases every GPU resource, observer and animation callback the viewer created; while the tab is hidden or the element is off screen the viewer does no per-frame work; a lost graphics context is restored or reported in the element.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green; test_leak_counters_catch_one_of_everything is the negative control. The hidden-tab and off-screen clauses are asserted on a fake DOM only, not in a real browser; real context loss is tested on the renderer page, not the viewer's in-element message.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/sample.test.js::criterion 2: output passes the contract loader; provenance says synthetic
evidence.behavior_text: The built-in producer's output is accepted by the contract loader; guide-producer and embeddings-cli export tests show the same for the two other producers; duplicate ids and a wrong block length are refused.
evidence.contract_text: Every data file states its schema version, model id, dimension, item count and where the vectors came from; every point has a stable id; all vectors have the stated dimension. A producer never emits a file that omits these.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: no viewer test refuses a file that omits model, dimension, count, provenance.source or a point id; 'a producer never emits' is shown for three known producers only.

evidence.behavior_text: A block of 9212 bytes is refused with the exact message naming the expected 6 x 384 x 4 = 9216 bytes; little-endian decoding, dtype, byte order and declared length are asserted by sibling tests.
evidence.contract_text: Vectors arrive as one little-endian float32 block whose length is exactly points x dimension x 4 bytes; a block of any other length is refused with a plain message.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green; these are the refusal cases themselves. No real-browser test of the wrong-length case (a wrong dtype is tested in Chromium).

evidence.test_ref: js/test/contract.test.js::criterion 1: bumped version names the version found and supported
evidence.behavior_text: The message says schema version 2 is not supported and that the viewer reads schema version 1; shown in Chromium by tests/browser/test_standalone_page.py::test_a_refused_set_shows_the_viewers_message_and_no_points.
evidence.contract_text: The viewer reads the schema version first and refuses an unknown or newer one, naming the version it found and the versions it supports.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: the code checks 'kind' before the version, so 'reads the schema version first' holds only relative to every other field; no test asserts the order against 'kind'.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/viewer.test.js::a refused append leaves the running view unchanged and shows a notice
evidence.behavior_text: An append with another dimension or model is refused (dimension-mismatch, model-mismatch); the set, the GPU count and the loop are unchanged.
evidence.contract_text: Data whose points disagree in dimension, or an append whose model id or dimension differs from what is already shown, is refused and the current view is left unchanged.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: 'points disagree in dimension' inside one set can only appear as a wrong block length (vectors are one flat block) and has no test of its own; no real-browser test of a refused append.

evidence.behavior_text: viewer serve with a sentinel key and address in its environment returns neither in any response; contract tests refuse a data file whose endpoint is an address; scan-secrets and the no-external-origin scan pass on shipped files.
evidence.contract_text: No page, shell or data file ever contains the gateway address or key, and the browser never contacts the gateway; the key exists only in the environment of the server-side process that embeds, placed there by grant run.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green with negative controls for the scans. Not covered by any test: 'the key exists only in the environment of the embedding process, placed there by grant run'. Its only support is the manual scan recorded in docs/evidence/2026-11-14-real-atlas-proof.md.

evidence.behavior_text: Data on another origin is refused without a request; after load the only requests are the data file and its block; the core file contains no network call (static scan).
evidence.contract_text: The viewer sends corpus text, labels, metadata and vectors nowhere; its only read is the data file or object its host handed it.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green; test_network_log_catches_a_request_to_another_origin (10 request kinds) is the negative control. Same-origin sends are excluded by the static scan only; no test inspects same-origin request bodies.

evidence.behavior_text: In Chromium at desktop and phone width the block shows model, dimension, count, 'Seed (view)' and the shadow sentence; test_markup_labels_are_literal_text asserts labels with markup create no element.
evidence.contract_text: Every mounted view shows source, model, dimension, item count, the seed, how the view is produced, and that a projection is a shadow of the space; labels and metadata are inserted as text only.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: the displayed value of the view seed is not firmly asserted (label only); a mounted viewer with no data shows no block by design; markup in metadata or provenance strings is untested; no negative control.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/math-tour.test.js::at 768-d the tour's reported variance share matches an independent recomputation
evidence.behavior_text: The reported share equals an independent recomputation at 384, 768, 1024 and 2560 dimensions; the status states it; after an append it is marked stale until refitted.
evidence.contract_text: The page states the share of total variance held by the directions the tour moves through, recomputed from the data shown, and never presents a guided view as the whole space.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. 'Never presents a guided view as the whole space' rests on two text assertions (Tumble's summary and the shadow sentence), not on a general check.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/modes-determinism.test.js::criterion 4: tumble at 1024-d gives bit-identical frames over 10 s in two fresh runs
evidence.behavior_text: 601 frames are byte-identical across two fresh runs for each mode; a different seed gives a different sequence.
evidence.contract_text: Given the same data, seed and elapsed time the frame is the same; the seed in use is always visible in the provenance block and can be set by the host.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green, with the different-seed test as the control. Partly covered: the seed's displayed value is asserted as a label only; a host-set seed is not checked end to end; no real-browser comparison across two loads.

evidence.test_ref: js/test/modes.test.js::criterion 2: a fourth dummy mode registers without editing any existing file
evidence.behavior_text: A fourth mode registers, the three shipped modes still give orthonormal frames, and every file under js/src (the contract included) is byte-identical afterwards.
evidence.contract_text: A mode supplies only its own motion and drawing rules over the shared projection, data and provenance; adding a fourth mode changes no existing mode and no part of the data contract.
evidence.strength_basis: Ran green. Partly covered: 'a mode supplies only its own motion and drawing rules' is not asserted (no scan of mode files).

evidence.behavior_text: Preview writes nothing; an existing target is refused without --force; a missing vector file is refused with a hint naming 'embeddings survey'; both files are staged then renamed; model, seed, limitations and uncertain are copied.
evidence.contract_text: It previews by default and writes nothing without --apply, refuses an existing target without --force, refuses an Atlas whose vector file is absent with a hint naming 'embeddings survey', writes atomically, and copies the Atlas's model, endpoint, seed, limitations and uncertain lists into the file's provenance.
